overview.label: Overview
overview.confirm: write a high-level overview of what they cover
overview.task: Synthesize an overview: the main themes across the documents, where they connect or conflict, and what the collection as a whole covers.

studyGuide.label: Study guide
studyGuide.confirm: build a study guide of the key concepts, terms, and review questions
studyGuide.task: Create a study guide from the documents: the key concepts and definitions, the most important points to remember, and a short list of self-check questions the documents themselves answer. Do not add questions the documents do not answer.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.confirm: draft frequently asked questions with answers drawn from them
faq.task: Write an FAQ from the documents: only questions the documents directly answer, each followed by a concise answer grounded in them. If the collection supports only a few such questions, produce fewer — do not invent plausible-sounding questions or answers.

timeline.label: Timeline
timeline.confirm: lay out the events and dates in chronological order
timeline.task: Build a chronological timeline of the dated events mentioned across the documents, earliest to latest, each line as "date — event". If the documents contain few dates, say so plainly.

briefing.label: Briefing
briefing.confirm: write a concise briefing of the most important points
briefing.task: Write a concise executive briefing: a one-paragraph summary, then the key findings as bullet points, then the implications or open questions. Draw every point from the documents; do not add outside context.

flashcards.label: Flashcards
flashcards.task: Create study flashcards from the documents as question/answer pairs, each formatted as "**Q:** …" on one line and "**A:** …" on the next line. Cover the most important facts the documents state; do not invent facts to fill more cards.

podcast.label: Audio Overview
podcast.confirm: write a two-host podcast dialogue about them (play it aloud with Read-aloud on)
podcast.task: Write a lively but accurate two-host podcast conversation about the collection, between hosts named Alex and Sam. Put each turn on its OWN line beginning with exactly "**Alex:**" or "**Sam:**" (start with Alex), and alternate between them. Open with a short hook, then discuss the main themes and how they connect in a natural back-and-forth — brief reactions, plain-language explanations, the occasional question from one host answered by the other — and close with a quick wrap-up. Keep each turn to a few sentences. Ground every statement in the summaries: do not invent facts, numbers, names, quotations, or events, and do not add outside context.
